items.title: What's on This Page
items.why:
One prize list for both kids' real prizes: Lennon's wish and Alice's encore. Mock-ups in the real app; nothing is built.

The list is plain data in one small file (js/rewards.js): a name and a kind (treat, outing, time together, other) per prize. Your rewards page can replace that file later. Each child's phone starts from it, and a grown-up can edit that phone's copy behind the passcode. Phones keep their own copy, because each profile syncs on its own.

items.title: The Starting List
items.why:
Treats: Ice cream from Culver's · Flan from Publix
Time together: Game night with Dad · Breakfast out with Dad · A movie night
Outings: A trip to the park · A trip to the library · Mini golf
Other: 30 minutes of extra screen time · Stay up 30 minutes late · A small toy

The American Academy of Pediatrics advises against food as a reward; the treats are in because you asked for them. I'd remove the "Please don't use food as a prize" line from the grown-up screens.

items.title: Lennon's Grown-Ups Screen
items.why: As built, a grown-up picks one prize for the next wish. The list becomes the editable one, with the edit link under it. "Type your own" goes away, since the editor does that.

items.title: Build It With Alice's Prize?
items.why: Lennon's kid mode (2.32.0) goes out first as you approved it, with the six-prize list and the "not food" line. This list then comes in 2.33.0 together with Alice's encore prize.
